TODAY IS 2026-09-29. Every "passed" or "expiring" judgement is against that date.

THE AGENCY THIS AUDIT IS ABOUT: Oregon DEQ
Only this agency. Another regulator's documents are listed at the end as titles only and
are not yours to judge here.

WHO THIS COMPANY IS
  Name: Cascade Specialty Chemicals, LLC
  Industry: chemical manufacturing (recorded as chemical-manufacturing)
  Address: Portland, Oregon
Their sites:
  - Portland — 4410 NW Front Ave, Portland, Oregon 97210 (primary)

DOCUMENTS ON FILE FOR OREGON DEQ — 5
Each is named by a HANDLE — D1, D2 — and that handle is how you refer to it. Nothing else.

  --- D1 — Air Permit Annual Report for 2025 (Standard ACDP 26-2841-ST-01) with Oregon DEQ Receipt Confirmation, Portland Facility
      file: 08-deq-annual-report-2025.pdf
      kind: record · status: recorded · shown as: recorded
      the document's own date: 2026-02-12 (issued)
      the date that matters: 2026-02-12 (last_entry)
      site: Portland
      what the reading said it is: This is your annual report on the Portland air permit for calendar year 2025, filed under Condition 4.1, plus DEQ's email confirming it was received on February 12, 2026. It is proof that the report was filed on time and a record of 2025 operations: throughput, the scrubber logs, C-1 carbon replacement, and one deviation that was reported. DEQ says plainly that the email confirms receipt only. It does not mean DEQ found the report complete or found the facility meeting its permit.
      WHAT THE READING FOUND WRONG WITH IT (1) — these are already findings; carry them, do not re-find them:
        · Confirm the C-1 carbon was replaced by March 14, 2026  [worked out from the document, not stated in it]
            The report says the next C-1 carbon replacement was due on or before March 14, 2026. That date passed more than six months ago. Nothing in this document shows it was done, and no replacement record for 2026 is in your files.
            what it needs: Find the 2026 carbon replacement record (vendor invoice or service ticket, date, carbon type and amount) and keep it with the permit records. If the carbon was not replaced on time, read Condition 3.3 and the deviation-reporting conditions (5.1/5.2) in the permit and decide whether DEQ needs to be told.
            the rule: Standard ACDP 26-2841-ST-01, Condition 3.3 (as named in the report; the permit's exact wording was not checked here)
      DATES THIS DOCUMENT SETS (3):
        · File the annual report for 2026 under Condition 4.1 (due date is set in the permit, not stated here) — no date stated (recurring)
        · Keep this confirmation and the permit records for five years (inferred: February 2031 counted from receipt) — 2031-02-12
        · Replace the carbon in unit C-1 (yearly schedule, according to the report) — 2026-03-14 (recurring)
      WHAT THE READING SAID A COMPANY LIKE THIS USUALLY ALSO HOLDS (7) —
        a suggestion from similar companies, NOT a checked requirement:
        · C-1 carbon replacement records for 2025 and 2026 (vendor invoices or service tickets) — These back up Condition 3.3 and the March 2026 due date.
        · Deviation report DEV-2025-0913 and DEQ's reply — The report refers to it, and it should sit in the permit file.
        · EPA TRI Form R submissions — Repackaging this much HCl, nitric acid, toluene and xylene may exceed TRI thresholds.
        · EPCRA Tier II inventory report / Oregon State Fire Marshal hazardous substance report — Acids, caustics and solvents are stored on site in large amounts.
        · Hazardous waste generator records (EPA ID, waste determinations, e.g. for spent carbon) — Spent solvent carbon and off-spec product usually produce regulated waste.
        · Industrial stormwater permit (Oregon DEQ 1200-Z) or a no-exposure certification — Industrial chemical sites in Oregon commonly hold one or the other.
        · Scrubber maintenance file with the 2025 quarterly inspection records (Condition 3.2) — The report says the inspections are kept in this file. It is the evidence behind the report.
      WHAT THIS DOCUMENT SAYS, proposed by the reading, not confirmed by anyone (5):
        · acid caustic repackaging lines: Acid line S-1 (hydrochloric, sulfuric, nitric acid solutions): 1,842,000 lb over 238 days in 2025. Caustic line S-2 (sodium and potassium hydroxide solutions): 1,210,000 lb over 231 days., as of 2025-12-31
            it says: "hydrochloric, sulfuric and nitric acid solutions"
            where: Page 2, Section 1 table
        · air permit deviations 2025: One deviation: S-2 recirculation pump failed August 22, 2025. DEQ notified August 23; written report sent September 2 (DEV-2025-0913)., as of 2025-12-31
            it says: "The Department was notified by email on August 23, 2025 and a written report was submitted on September 2, 2025"
            where: Page 3, Section 4
        · air permit type and number: Standard Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01, as of 2026-02-10
            it says: "Standard Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01"
            where: Page 2, header
        · carbon adsorption unit c1: Carbon last replaced March 14, 2025 (Calgon Filtrasorb 400, 1,800 lb, Northwest Carbon Services). Outlet checked weekly by detector tube; no breakthrough in 2025., as of 2025-12-31
            it says: "The carbon in C-1 was replaced on March 14, 2025 (Calgon Filtrasorb 400, 1,800 pounds, by Northwest Carbon Services)."
            where: Page 3, Section 3
        · solvent bulk storage: Tanks T-3 to T-6 hold acetone, isopropanol, toluene and xylene, vented through C-1. 3,960,000 gallons received in 2025., as of 2025-12-31
            it says: "acetone, isopropanol, toluene, xylene"
            where: Page 2, Section 1 table

  --- D2 — Monthly EHS Self-Check Form (blank internal template), Portland Facility
      file: 13-company-self-check.docx
      kind: other · status: not_judged · shown as: on_file
      the document's own date: none stated (unknown)
      the date that matters: none
      site: Portland
      what the reading said it is: This is the company's own blank monthly checklist. It has eight lines covering the air permit, the scrubber and carbon-unit logs, forklift inspections, fire extinguishers, exits, eyewash stations and showers, and safety data sheets. It is a template, not a filled-in record, so it proves nothing yet. It becomes evidence only when someone completes it each month with Y/N, initials and a supervisor sign-off.
      WHAT THE READING FOUND WRONG WITH IT: nothing
      DATES THIS DOCUMENT SETS (1):
        · Report any items marked N to the Plant Manager — no date stated (recurring)
      WHAT THE READING SAID A COMPANY LIKE THIS USUALLY ALSO HOLDS (6) —
        a suggestion from similar companies, NOT a checked requirement:
        · Completed monthly self-checks for recent months — The blank form shows the process exists. Completed, signed copies are what show it was actually done.
        · Exit route and exit sign inspection records — Line 6 checks exits and exit signs. Sites like this often keep a separate record of emergency lighting and exit sign tests.
        · Hazardous waste generator records and Oregon Community Right-to-Know / Tier II hazardous substance reporting — Chemical repackagers with bulk storage and tank farms usually hold these.
        · OSHA Form 300 Log and Form 301 incident reports for 2025 — The company holds the 300A summary but not the log or incident reports behind it.
        · Weekly eyewash and safety shower activation log — Line 7 refers to a log for eyewash and shower flushing, and it is not in what the company holds.
        · Written Hazard Communication program, plus a chemical inventory / SDS binder index — Line 8 refers to an SDS binder index. No written HazCom program appears in what the company holds, and chemical makers and repackagers usually keep one.
      WHAT THIS DOCUMENT SAYS, proposed by the reading, not confirmed by anyone (2):
        · emergency eyewash shower location: There is more than one eyewash station and safety shower at the site. The form does not say where they are.
            it says: "Eyewash stations and safety showers flushed this week and logged"
            where: Line 7
        · scrubber pressure drop range: The form's acceptable range for scrubber pressure drop is 2.0 to 6.0. No units are given.
            it says: "readings between 2.0 and 6.0"
            where: Line 2

  --- D3 — Oregon DEQ Air Contaminant Discharge Permit Compliance Inspection Checklist (Inspector's Field Form), blank
      file: 12-auditor-checklist-deq-air.docx
      kind: other · status: not_judged · shown as: on_file
      the document's own date: none stated (unknown)
      the date that matters: none
      site: Portland
      what the reading said it is: This is a blank inspection checklist, not a permit, record or program. Every field is empty: facility, permit number, inspection date, inspector, all Yes/No/N.A. answers, evidence, notes and signatures. It proves nothing about Cascade yet. Its real use is as a list of what an inspector would ask to see. Lines A1–C5 cover the permit, renewal timing, annual and semi-annual reports, deviation reporting, scrubber and carbon-unit records, opacity monitoring, keeping records for 5 years, and conditions on the day of inspection.
      WHAT THE READING FOUND WRONG WITH IT: nothing
      DATES THIS DOCUMENT SETS (4):
        · Annual report for calendar year 2026 (the form says it is due by February 15; confirm the date in the permit) — 2027-02-15 (recurring)
        · Deviation reporting: notify within 24 hours and report in writing within 15 days of any deviation (according to the form; confirm in the permit) — no date stated (recurring)
        · Permit renewal application: the form says at least 120 days before expiry. Confirm the lead time in the permit and in OAR 340-216; I am not sure 120 days is right for a Standard ACDP. — no date stated (recurring)
        · Semi-annual monitoring report for January–June 2026 (the form says it was due July 31, which has passed; check that it was filed, and confirm in the permit that such a report is required) — 2026-07-31 (recurring)
      WHAT THE READING SAID A COMPANY LIKE THIS USUALLY ALSO HOLDS (7) —
        a suggestion from similar companies, NOT a checked requirement:
        · Carbon replacement or breakthrough record for unit C-1 from the last 12 months — Line B3 asks for it; the documents held include only the weekly detector-tube check.
        · Deviation reports and DEQ notifications from the last 12 months, or a written statement that none occurred — Line A5 asks for them; the company already tracks air_permit_deviations_2025.
        · Opacity (visible emissions) observation records, or a written statement of the monitoring method — Line B5 asks for one or the other.
        · Quarterly scrubber inspection records for the last four quarters (S-1 acid line, S-2 caustic line) — Line B2 asks for them; the documents held include only the daily pressure-drop log.
        · Records retention procedure (5 years) — Line B6 asks whether records are kept for 5 years and available on request.
        · Scrubber pressure-drop log covering the full last 12 months — Line B1 asks for 12 months; the log held covers only August–September 2026.
        · Semi-annual monitoring report for January–June 2026, with proof DEQ received it — Line A4 asks for it and it is not among the documents held.

  --- D4 — Scrubber Pressure-Drop Log (S-1 acid line, S-2 caustic line) and Weekly C-1 Carbon Outlet Detector-Tube Check, August–September 2026, Portland Facility
      file: 07-scrubber-log-record.pdf
      kind: record · status: gaps_found · shown as: needs_work
      the document's own date: 2026-09-25 (last_entry)
      the date that matters: 2026-09-25 (last_entry)
      site: Portland
      what the reading said it is: This is your own monitoring log. It records the checks required by Conditions 3.1 and 3.3 of your Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01: a daily pressure-drop reading on scrubbers S-1 and S-2, and a weekly breakthrough check at the outlet of carbon unit C-1. It is judged on whether it is complete and up to date. It has four problems: operating days with no reading in August, a September 9 reading above the permit range with nothing noted about it, a missing weekly carbon check in September, and no supervisor sign-off.
      WHAT THE READING FOUND WRONG WITH IT (4) — these are already findings; carry them, do not re-find them:
        · Five August operating days have no scrubber reading
            The log's own line counters say the acid line ran 21 days and the caustic line ran 20 days in August, but only 16 rows are entered. There are no entries at all between August 14 and August 24. The weekly carbon check on August 17 shows the site was working that week. That leaves about 5 operating days with no reading for S-1 and 5 for S-2. Condition 3.1 requires a reading every operating day.
            what it needs: Check whether readings for August 17–21 were taken on paper or another sheet and never copied in. If they were not taken, write a dated note in the log explaining the missed days. Check your permit's deviation and annual-report terms to see whether missed monitoring has to be reported to Oregon DEQ. Consider matching the log against the line counters every week.
            the rule: Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01, Condition 3.1 (as quoted in the log header)
        · September 9 S-2 reading above the permit range, with nothing recorded about it
            On September 9 scrubber S-2 read 6.4 inches of water column. The permit range is 2.0 to 6.0. The Notes column is blank: no cause, no corrective action, no time it was back in range. The next day's reading was 4.6.
            what it needs: Add a dated note giving the cause, what was done (for example, nozzles cleaned), and when the reading came back into range. Check your permit for any requirement to record or report an excursion from a parameter range, and file with Oregon DEQ if it applies. I have not read the permit's reporting conditions, so I cannot say whether a report is required.
            the rule: Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01, Condition 3.1. Any reporting duty would be in the permit's own reporting conditions, which I have not seen.
        · Weekly C-1 carbon outlet check missing for the week of September 14
            Condition 3.3 requires a breakthrough check at the C-1 outlet every week. September shows checks only for the weeks of September 7 and September 21. There is none for the week of September 14, even though the lines ran September 14–18. The week of September 28 is still in progress.
            what it needs: Find out whether the check was done and not written down. If it was not done, note the missed week in the log, consider whether it has to be reported under the permit, and make sure the week of September 28 check gets done.
            the rule: Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01, Condition 3.3 (as quoted in the log)
        · No supervisor review signature
            The form has a line for supervisor review, but it is blank with no date. That leaves no sign that anyone reviewed the log, which may be why the missing days and the 6.4 reading went unnoticed.
            what it needs: Have a supervisor review both months, record what they find, then sign and date. Make it a monthly review.
      DATES THIS DOCUMENT SETS (2):
        · Record the S-1 and S-2 pressure drop each day either line runs — no date stated (recurring)
        · Weekly C-1 carbon outlet breakthrough check (week of Sep 28 is still due) — 2026-10-02 (recurring)
      WHAT THE READING SAID A COMPANY LIKE THIS USUALLY ALSO HOLDS (4) —
        a suggestion from similar companies, NOT a checked requirement:
        · C-1 carbon change-out records — Usually kept alongside breakthrough checks to show when the carbon was replaced.
        · Earlier monthly logs and annual report submitted to Oregon DEQ under the permit — Permits like this usually require keeping monitoring records for several years and reporting yearly.
        · Magnehelic gauge calibration or check records — Supports whether the pressure readings can be trusted.
        · Scrubber maintenance and corrective-action log — Would show what was done about the September 9 excursion and routine work like the August 14 nozzle rinse.
      WHAT THIS DOCUMENT SAYS, proposed by the reading, not confirmed by anyone (3):
        · acid caustic repackaging lines: Acid repackaging line controlled by scrubber S-1; caustic repackaging line controlled by scrubber S-2, as of 2026-09-25
            it says: "S-1 (acid repackaging line) and S-2 (caustic repackaging line)"
            where: Page 1, header
        · air permit type and number: Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01, as of 2026-09-25
            it says: "Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01, Condition 3.1"
            where: Page 1, header
        · carbon adsorption unit c1: Carbon adsorption unit C-1 on site, with a weekly outlet breakthrough check, as of 2026-09-25
            it says: "weekly check for breakthrough at the C-1 carbon unit outlet"
            where: Page 1, weekly C-1 section

  --- D5 — Standard Air Contaminant Discharge Permit No. 26-2841-ST-01, Portland Facility
      file: 02-acdp-chemical.pdf
      kind: permit · status: expiring · shown as: expiring
      the document's own date: 2021-09-01 (issued)
      the date that matters: 2026-11-15 (expiry)
      site: Portland
      what the reading said it is: This is Oregon DEQ's Standard Air Contaminant Discharge Permit (ACDP). It allows the Portland facility to run two acid/caustic scrubbers and four solvent tanks that vent to a carbon unit. Because it is the agency's own document, there is nothing in it for you to fix. What matters is keeping the daily, weekly, quarterly and annual monitoring records, filing the reports on time, and getting it renewed. It expires on November 15, 2026, 47 days from today. The renewal application was due July 18, 2026, which has already passed, so the first thing to check is whether a complete renewal application went in by that date.
      WHAT THE READING FOUND WRONG WITH IT: nothing
      WHAT THIS DOCUMENT OBLIGES THEM TO KEEP DOING (14), read out of the document itself:
        · 1.1 — Operate the sources in Section 2 under all permit conditions and all applicable DEQ rules
            the evidence you would expect to see: The permit on file plus the monitoring and reporting records listed below.
        · 1.2 — Do not run the permitted sources after November 15, 2026, without a renewed permit or a timely renewal application
            the evidence you would expect to see: The renewed permit, or proof of a timely renewal application.
        · 1.3 — Submit a complete renewal application on or before July 18, 2026 (120 days before expiry)
            the evidence you would expect to see: A copy of the submitted renewal application and DEQ's receipt or acknowledgment showing a date on or before July 18, 2026.
        · 1.4 — Notify DEQ in writing at least 60 days before any change in ownership, and before any source modification that would increase emissions
            the evidence you would expect to see: Copies of written notices to DEQ, or a note that no ownership change or modification occurred.
        · 3.1 — Keep pressure drop across scrubbers S-1 and S-2 between 2.0 and 6.0 in. water column while their lines operate, and record it once per operating day
            the evidence you would expect to see: A scrubber log with daily pressure-drop readings for S-1 and S-2 on every operating day.
        · 3.2 — Inspect each scrubber's recirculation pump, spray nozzles, packing and mist eliminator at least once per calendar quarter
            the evidence you would expect to see: Quarterly scrubber log entries showing the date, the inspector and any corrective action.
        · 3.3 — Replace the carbon in unit C-1 at least every 12 months, or sooner if the weekly detector-tube check at the C-1 outlet shows breakthrough
            the evidence you would expect to see: Weekly detector-tube check records and carbon replacement records (dates, vendor invoices or manifests).
        · 3.4 — Keep visible emissions from any permitted source at or below 20% opacity, except for periods totaling no more than three minutes in any hour
            the evidence you would expect to see: Visible-emissions observation records, or no-visible-emissions notes, and any excess-emission reports.
        · 4.1 — Submit an annual report by February 15 covering the prior calendar year
            the evidence you would expect to see: Submitted annual reports with throughput by line, scrubber log summaries, carbon replacement dates and excess emission events.
        · 4.2 — Submit a semi-annual monitoring report by July 31 covering January through June
            the evidence you would expect to see: Submitted semi-annual reports, including the one due July 31, 2026, with proof of submittal.
        · 4.3 — Keep all records the permit requires for at least five years and make them available to DEQ
            the evidence you would expect to see: An organized five-year record archive (logs, reports, carbon records).
        · 5.1 — Minimize emissions during scrubber malfunction, including stopping the associated repackaging line
            the evidence you would expect to see: Malfunction and shutdown records in the scrubber log.
        · 5.2 — Notify DEQ within 24 hours of discovering any deviation, and send a written report within 15 days
            the evidence you would expect to see: Deviation notification emails or call logs, plus the 15-day written reports.
        · 6.2 — Pay the annual permit fee by the invoice due date
            the evidence you would expect to see: DEQ fee invoices and proof of payment.
      DATES THIS DOCUMENT SETS (6):
        · Annual permit fee — no date stated (recurring)
        · Annual report for calendar year 2026 — 2027-02-15 (recurring)
        · Carbon replacement in C-1 (at least every 12 months; date depends on the last replacement) — no date stated (recurring)
        · Permit expiration — 2026-11-15
        · Renewal application due (date has passed; confirm it was filed) — 2026-07-18
        · Semi-annual monitoring report (January to June); next one after the July 31, 2026 report — 2027-07-31 (recurring)
      WHAT THE READING SAID A COMPANY LIKE THIS USUALLY ALSO HOLDS (6) —
        a suggestion from similar companies, NOT a checked requirement:
        · Hazard Communication program and chemical inventory (plus EPCRA Tier II filing, if thresholds are met) — The site handles bulk acids, caustics and solvents.
        · Hazardous waste generator registration and records (spent carbon, off-spec product) — Spent carbon and chemical waste are typical waste streams for this kind of operation.
        · Industrial stormwater permit (Oregon 1200-Z) or no-exposure certification — Chemical manufacturing and repackaging sites in Oregon commonly hold one.
        · Proof of a timely ACDP renewal application — This is the only thing that allows operation past November 15, 2026, if DEQ has not yet issued a new permit.
        · Recent annual and semi-annual ACDP reports — Conditions 4.1 and 4.2 require them; the July 31, 2026 report should already be on file.
        · Scrubber log and C-1 carbon/detector-tube records — Conditions 3.1–3.3 require them, and DEQ can ask for five years of them.
      WHAT THIS DOCUMENT SAYS, proposed by the reading, not confirmed by anyone (4):
        · acid caustic repackaging lines: An acid repackaging line (scrubber S-1) and a caustic repackaging line (scrubber S-2), as of 2021-09-01
            it says: "Packed-bed wet scrubber S-1 serving the acid repackaging line (design flow 4,500 scfm)."
            where: Section 2.1–2.2, page 3
        · air permit type and number: Oregon DEQ Standard ACDP 26-2841-ST-01, as of 2021-09-01
            it says: "Permit number: 26-2841-ST-01"
            where: Page 1
        · solvent bulk storage: Four 10,000-gallon fixed-roof solvent tanks (T-3 to T-6), vented to carbon unit C-1, as of 2021-09-01
            it says: "Solvent storage tanks T-3, T-4, T-5 and T-6 (each 10,000 gallons, fixed roof, vented to carbon adsorption unit C-1)."
            where: Section 2.3, page 3
        · source category: Chemical storage and repackaging with vapor control, as of 2021-09-01
            it says: "Source category: Chemical storage and repackaging with vapor control"
            where: Page 1

documents.title: Scrubber Pressure-Drop Log (S-1 acid line, S-2 caustic line) and Weekly C-1 Carbon Outlet Detector-Tube Check, August–September 2026, Portland Facility
documents.summary: This is your own monitoring log. It records the checks required by Conditions 3.1 and 3.3 of your Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01: a daily pressure-drop reading on scrubbers S-1 and S-2, and a weekly breakthrough check at the outlet of carbon unit C-1. It is judged on whether it is complete and up to date. It has four problems: operating days with no reading in August, a September 9 reading above the permit range with nothing noted about it, a missing weekly carbon check in September, and no supervisor sign-off.

open_gaps.title: Five August operating days have no scrubber reading
open_gaps.description: The log's own line counters say the acid line ran 21 days and the caustic line ran 20 days in August, but only 16 rows are entered. There are no entries at all between August 14 and August 24. The weekly carbon check on August 17 shows the site was working that week. That leaves about 5 operating days with no reading for S-1 and 5 for S-2. Condition 3.1 requires a reading every operating day.
open_gaps.fix: Check whether readings for August 17–21 were taken on paper or another sheet and never copied in. If they were not taken, write a dated note in the log explaining the missed days. Check your permit's deviation and annual-report terms to see whether missed monitoring has to be reported to Oregon DEQ. Consider matching the log against the line counters every week.
open_gaps.citation: Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01, Condition 3.1 (as quoted in the log header)

open_gaps.title: September 9 S-2 reading above the permit range, with nothing recorded about it
open_gaps.description: On September 9 scrubber S-2 read 6.4 inches of water column. The permit range is 2.0 to 6.0. The Notes column is blank: no cause, no corrective action, no time it was back in range. The next day's reading was 4.6.
open_gaps.fix: Add a dated note giving the cause, what was done (for example, nozzles cleaned), and when the reading came back into range. Check your permit for any requirement to record or report an excursion from a parameter range, and file with Oregon DEQ if it applies. I have not read the permit's reporting conditions, so I cannot say whether a report is required.
open_gaps.citation: Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01, Condition 3.1. Any reporting duty would be in the permit's own reporting conditions, which I have not seen.

open_gaps.title: Weekly C-1 carbon outlet check missing for the week of September 14
open_gaps.description: Condition 3.3 requires a breakthrough check at the C-1 outlet every week. September shows checks only for the weeks of September 7 and September 21. There is none for the week of September 14, even though the lines ran September 14–18. The week of September 28 is still in progress.
open_gaps.fix: Find out whether the check was done and not written down. If it was not done, note the missed week in the log, consider whether it has to be reported under the permit, and make sure the week of September 28 check gets done.
open_gaps.citation: Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01, Condition 3.3 (as quoted in the log)

open_gaps.title: No supervisor review signature
open_gaps.description: The form has a line for supervisor review, but it is blank with no date. That leaves no sign that anyone reviewed the log, which may be why the missing days and the 6.4 reading went unnoticed.
open_gaps.fix: Have a supervisor review both months, record what they find, then sign and date. Make it a monthly review.

documents.title: Standard Air Contaminant Discharge Permit No. 26-2841-ST-01, Portland Facility
documents.summary: This is Oregon DEQ's Standard Air Contaminant Discharge Permit (ACDP). It allows the Portland facility to run two acid/caustic scrubbers and four solvent tanks that vent to a carbon unit. Because it is the agency's own document, there is nothing in it for you to fix. What matters is keeping the daily, weekly, quarterly and annual monitoring records, filing the reports on time, and getting it renewed. It expires on November 15, 2026, 47 days from today. The renewal application was due July 18, 2026, which has already passed, so the first thing to check is whether a complete renewal application went in by that date.

conditions.title: Operate the sources in Section 2 under all permit conditions and all applicable DEQ rules
conditions.evidence_expected: The permit on file plus the monitoring and reporting records listed below.

conditions.title: Do not run the permitted sources after November 15, 2026, without a renewed permit or a timely renewal application
conditions.evidence_expected: The renewed permit, or proof of a timely renewal application.

conditions.title: Submit a complete renewal application on or before July 18, 2026 (120 days before expiry)
conditions.evidence_expected: A copy of the submitted renewal application and DEQ's receipt or acknowledgment showing a date on or before July 18, 2026.

conditions.title: Notify DEQ in writing at least 60 days before any change in ownership, and before any source modification that would increase emissions

conditions.title: Keep pressure drop across scrubbers S-1 and S-2 between 2.0 and 6.0 in. water column while their lines operate, and record it once per operating day

conditions.title: Inspect each scrubber's recirculation pump, spray nozzles, packing and mist eliminator at least once per calendar quarter
conditions.evidence_expected: Quarterly scrubber log entries showing the date, the inspector and any corrective action.

conditions.title: Replace the carbon in unit C-1 at least every 12 months, or sooner if the weekly detector-tube check at the C-1 outlet shows breakthrough
conditions.evidence_expected: Weekly detector-tube check records and carbon replacement records (dates, vendor invoices or manifests).

conditions.title: Keep visible emissions from any permitted source at or below 20% opacity, except for periods totaling no more than three minutes in any hour
conditions.evidence_expected: Visible-emissions observation records, or no-visible-emissions notes, and any excess-emission reports.

conditions.title: Submit an annual report by February 15 covering the prior calendar year
conditions.evidence_expected: Submitted annual reports with throughput by line, scrubber log summaries, carbon replacement dates and excess emission events.

conditions.title: Submit a semi-annual monitoring report by July 31 covering January through June
conditions.evidence_expected: Submitted semi-annual reports, including the one due July 31, 2026, with proof of submittal.

conditions.title: Keep all records the permit requires for at least five years and make them available to DEQ
conditions.evidence_expected: An organized five-year record archive (logs, reports, carbon records).

conditions.title: Minimize emissions during scrubber malfunction, including stopping the associated repackaging line
conditions.evidence_expected: Malfunction and shutdown records in the scrubber log.

conditions.title: Notify DEQ within 24 hours of discovering any deviation, and send a written report within 15 days
conditions.evidence_expected: Deviation notification emails or call logs, plus the 15-day written reports.

conditions.evidence_expected: DEQ fee invoices and proof of payment.
